details: CONFIRMED by a reproduction on the repo's fixtures. gate_runs (lib/relay_gate_watch.py:152-153) removes every run file of `sha`
before the first gate call; on Unavailable at k == 0 it returns with nothing written. Before this change the watch wrote its
file only when an end line arrived and never removed one, so a failed re-watch kept the last result. The docstring still says
"written when an end line arrives (and only then)". Same code path for the twin folder.
Size: 15 min.
evidence: scratchpad/cmpmeasure/test_repro_stale.py (watch green, then watch with Unavailable):
failing_case: Watch of master tip T ends green (T.remote.gate.log, exit 0). The host then goes down and the owner (or a second watch on the
same tip, as the stop-sending message invites: "gates stay on this Mac until a Linux watch there finishes") runs
`relay gate --watch-default` again. gate_runs removes T's run files first, then the gate raises Unavailable.
Now: run_files(folder, T) == [] and newest_watch() returns None (or an older commit's file, possibly an old red one), so
build_remote says "has not yet gated the default branch" or shows a stale red; the comparison loses T's pair.
Should: T keeps its green file until a new run of T has an end line.
fix_hint: Remove the stale runs only after the first new run returned a result (just before writing run 0), not before the gate call.
pass_cases: 1. watch [green] on T, then watch on T with gate raising Unavailable: run_files(folder, T) is [T.remote.gate.log] and newest_watch(wt)[0] == T with code 0.
2. watch [red, red] on T, then watch [green] on T: only T.remote.gate.log, exit 0 (tests/test_gate_compare.py:297 keeps passing).
3. watch [red, green] on T: two files, default_red "" (tests/test_gate_compare.py:262 keeps passing).
4. twin of J that cannot run on a second try keeps the first twin's file.
findings.summary: a new gating of a commit deletes its earlier Linux result before the host answers; a re-watch that cannot run leaves no result

details: CONFIRMED by a reproduction. linux_result reads committed build-time logs from os.path.join(main, ".relay/checks"), the main
checkout's working tree, which is on the default branch. A red landing's branch never reached the default branch, so its
committed remote logs are only in the branch's commits; the check never sees them. Test 11
(tests/test_gate_compare.py:387) passes only because it writes the log as an untracked file into the main checkout, which no
real gate does: the test passes with the behaviour absent. Effect: the "no twin when a remote log exists" rule never fires in
practice (one redundant VPS gate per such red landing, the waste the design's F5 removed), and until a twin result exists the
comparison shows those red landings as unresolved. mac_next already reads logs with `git show <ref>:<path>`; the same is needed
here.
Size: 20 min.
evidence: scratchpad/cmpmeasure/test_repro_branchlog.py (log committed in the branch worktree, red(judged=that commit)):
failing_case: Branch wt/x: code commit B, then its build-time remote gate log committed on the branch (.relay/checks/B.remote.gate.log in
commit C, only an inert file). The landing judges C (the take brought nothing or only inert files) and goes red; red done event
judged = C. start_twin_after_landing(main, C) spawns a twin, and linux_result(main, C, (master, wt/x)) is None, so the
comparison shows "no Linux result: C (red landing)".
Should (design 7.3, decision 1, test 11): the stretch of C has a Linux result (B's log), so no twin starts and the pair comes
from that log.
fix_hint: For the committed-log place, read `.relay/checks/<commit>.remote.gate.log` (and its re-runs) with `git show <sha>:<path>` and
`git show <ref>:<path>` for the refs passed (the log is committed after the commit it names, so read it from the later commits
of the stretch or the ref tips), instead of the working tree. Rewrite test 11 to commit the log on the branch.
pass_cases: 1. The failing case: log committed on the branch only (not in the main checkout): start_twin_after_landing spawns nothing; compare_lines shows "0 landed, 1 red landings; 1 agree" for an exit-1 log.
2. Same with the log exit 0: no twin; verdict is a Mac-only red (not "no Linux result").
3. A landed head whose remote log came in with the landing (file present on master): still pairs (tests/test_gate_compare.py:150).
4. A red landing whose take brought code from master (stretch of J stops at J): the twin still starts.
reason: tests/test_gate_compare.py Twin tests on branch-committed logs pass, fail at base.
findings.summary: a branch's committed build-time remote log is looked for only in the main checkout's working tree, so a red landing always gets a twin and its pair misses that log

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Design 7.4 makes "the newest run" the state and the fix item conditional on the last re-run being red;
it did not foresee a no-verdict re-run. The code treats 124 (and codes >= 127) like a green re-run in both newest_watch and
gate_runs, which turns an unconfirmed red into a clean default branch. A hang-type Linux failure is exactly the case where the
second run hits the limit.
Size: 15 min.
evidence: gate_runs: `if not is_red(result.code): break` then `return lines, last, path, True`;
gate_commit: `if complete and last is not None and is_red(last.code)`;
newest_watch: `files = run_files(folder, sha)` ... `return sha, _exit_code(lines), files[-1], age`;
build_remote: `if is_red(code):` sets red, else red "".
failing_case: Watch of tip T: run 0 exit 1 (red), re-run 1 exit 124 (stopped at its limit, no verdict). gate_runs stops the loop (124 is
not red) with complete=True; gate_commit files nothing (is_red(124) is False); newest_watch reads the re-run file (124), so
build_remote sets default_red "" and lane gates go to the VPS whose default branch was just seen red. The comparison shows
"no Linux result". Should: a re-run with no verdict confirms nothing; the red first run stays the state (default_red set, as
when a re-run cannot run, tests/test_gate_compare.py:291).
fix_hint: In gate_runs, a run that is neither 0 nor red ends the loop with complete=False; newest_watch (and linux_result) take the
newest run with a verdict (0 or red).
pass_cases: 1. watch [1, 124]: no fix item filed, build_remote(...).default_red != "" (the red run stands, like the could-not-run case).
3. watch [1, 1]: one fix item (tests/test_gate_compare.py:274 keeps passing).
4. watch [124] alone: no fix item, default_red "" (today's behaviour for a first-run stop).
findings.summary: a red watch whose re-run stops at the time limit (124) or is killed clears the red: no fix item, lanes go back to the VPS

details: CONFIRMED by reading: mac_next returns only the exit code; _entry maps any red code to MAC_RED. Size: 15 min.
failing_case: Red landing J failed at step "library tests"; a later Mac gate of the same code is red at step "lint" (a different, unrelated
break). Now: "Mac-only red, reproduced on the Mac", which breaks the streak. Design 7.2/test 15: reproduced only with the same
first step.
fix_hint: Return the later log's first failing step from mac_next and compare it with the red landing log's (J.gate.log) first step.
pass_cases: 1. later Mac gate red at the same first step: "reproduced on the Mac".
2. later Mac gate red at another step: not "reproduced" (shown as unresolved or as a separate verdict).
3. later Mac gate green: "flaky on the Mac" (tests/test_gate_compare.py:173).
findings.summary: a later red Mac gate of the same code counts as 'reproduced on the Mac' whatever step failed
